population.definition: Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC), the council area of the Federal Capital Territory that contains the city of Abuja, 2006 census as tabulated by the National Bureau of Statistics

source.title: Annual Abstract of Statistics, 2010 (Table 52: Population of FCT, Abuja by Council Area, 1991 and 2006)

facts.claim: The Federal Capital Territory had 1,406,239 inhabitants in the 2006 census, across six council areas.

source.title: Annual Abstract of Statistics, 2010 (Table 52: Population of FCT, Abuja by Council Area, 1991 and 2006)

facts.claim: Abuja Municipal Area Council grew from 226,949 inhabitants in 1991 to 776,298 in 2006.

source.title: Annual Abstract of Statistics, 2010 (Table 52: Population of FCT, Abuja by Council Area, 1991 and 2006)

facts.claim: The Abuja site was chosen as a more neutral and more central location for Nigeria's many ethnic and religious groups.

source.title: Nigeria@60: Why Nigeria's capital was moved from Lagos to Abuja
source.author: Lois Ugbede
source.quote: The choice of Abuja was made as it was seen as a more neutral land for Nigeria’s many ethnic and religious groups and as a more central location in the country

facts.claim: The site was inhabited by several ethnic groups, such as the Gbagyi, Koro, Gade and Gwandara, none of them among the dominant nationalities Hausa, Igbo, Yoruba and Ijaw.

source.title: Nigeria@60: Why Nigeria's capital was moved from Lagos to Abuja
source.author: Lois Ugbede
source.quote: Abuja was a site in the center of the country inhabited by several ethnic groups like the Gbagyi, Koro, Gade, and Gwandara, none of which belongs to the dominant nationalities: Hausa, Igbo, Yoruba, and Ijaw

facts.claim: The decision to build the new capital displaced the native residents of old Abuja, and the displacement remains controversial.

source.title: Nigeria@60: Why Nigeria's capital was moved from Lagos to Abuja
source.author: Lois Ugbede
source.quote: This decision, however, led to the displacement of the native people who were residents of the old Abuja

facts.claim: Aso Rock is the highest geographical point of the Federal Capital City and was used as the reference point for the first concept plan drawn by International Planning Associates for the Abuja Master Plan.

source.title: The contemporary and historical Aso Rock
source.author: Umar Shuaibu
source.quote: the Aso Rock was used as the reference point while drawing the first concept plan for the development of the city by the International Planning Associates (IPA), while producing the Abuja Master Plan

facts.claim: The aesthetics of the surrounding hills (Suleja, Zuma-Bwari-Aso, Karu-Agwai and Zango-Kuku) also guided the choice of the city's site.

source.title: The Natural Landmarks Of Abuja And National Monuments
source.quote: The aesthetics of the surrounding Suleja hills to the west, Zuma-Bwari-Aso hills to its north, Karu-Agwai hills to the east and the Zango-Kuku hills to the south also guided the site selection for the city’s location

facts.claim: The Abuja National Mosque is the largest mosque in Nigeria, according to the Nigerian press.

source.title: 6 largest mosques in Nigeria
source.quote: The Abuja National Mosque, also known as the Nigerian National Mosque, is the largest in Nigeria

timeline.claim: General Murtala Mohammed announced that Abuja would be developed as the new capital.

source.title: Nigeria@60: Why Nigeria's capital was moved from Lagos to Abuja
source.author: Lois Ugbede
source.quote: In 1976, the then head of state, General Murtala Mohammed announced that Abuja would be developed as the new capital

timeline.claim: The Abuja National Mosque Council was inaugurated by the Sultan of Sokoto, Abubakar III, as the mosque project began.

source.title: Nigeria's Abuja National Mosque: A Symbol of Faith, Culture, and Unity
source.author: Ruwanthi Abeyakoon
source.quote: In 1981, the Abuja National Mosque Council was inaugurated by Sultan Abubakar III of Sokoto

timeline.claim: The Abuja National Mosque was completed, according to a Nigerian press list of the largest mosques.

source.title: 6 largest mosques in Nigeria
source.quote: it was completed in 1984 and can accommodate up to 25,000 worshippers

timeline.claim: Abuja became the new capital of Nigeria in December 1991, after construction began in the 1980s.

source.title: Nigeria@60: Why Nigeria's capital was moved from Lagos to Abuja
source.author: Lois Ugbede
source.quote: Construction started in the 1980s and Abuja became the new capital in December 1991

places.name: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove
places.what: The grove lies on the Osun River just outside Osogbo, in south-west Nigeria, far from Abuja. It is dedicated to the Yoruba goddess Osun and is one of only two UNESCO World Heritage sites in Nigeria.

facts.label: Dedicated to
facts.value: Osun, Yoruba goddess of love and fertility, said to dwell in the river

source.title: On the brink: Inside the project to save Osun Oshogbo
source.quote: in the river runs Osun, goddess of love and fertility

facts.label: Age and rarity
facts.value: Founded some 400 years ago; the largest sacred grove to have survived the spread of Christianity and Islam in Nigeria

source.title: On the brink: Inside the project to save Osun Oshogbo
source.quote: Founded some 400 years ago, it’s the largest sacred grove to have survived the spread of Christianity and Islam in Nigeria

facts.label: Size
facts.value: 75 hectares, on the banks of the Osun River in Osogbo

source.title: Sacred Groves
source.quote: the 75 hectare Sacred Groves located in the town of Osogbo on the banks of the Osun River is the last example of its kind

source.title: Sacred Groves
source.quote: In 2005, UNESCO recognised its outstanding universal value by designating the Sacred Groves a World Heritage site

places.what: Nigeria's national mosque, in the capital, is known for its golden dome and four minarets. The Nigerian press calls it the country's largest mosque.

places.name: National Christian Centre
places.what: The National Christian Centre was first known as the National Ecumenical Centre. A Daily Trust opinion piece says it remained under construction for more than 20 years and that a government move to complete it was contested.

source.title: The National Mosque Still Stands
source.quote: the building of the National Ecumenical Centre that had remained under construction for more than 20 years

facts.label: Construction
facts.value: Under construction for more than 20 years after the National Mosque was built

source.title: The National Mosque Still Stands
source.quote: the National Ecumenical Centre that had remained under construction for more than 20 years after the National Mosque was designed, built and commissioned

facts.label: Controversy
facts.value: The Emir of Gwandu, then chairman of the National Mosque board, objected to a government move to complete it

source.title: The National Mosque Still Stands
source.quote: It was His Royal Highness, Alhaji Mustapha Jokolo, the then Emir of Gwandu that confronted Obasanjo over the government’s clandestine move to complete the building of the National Ecumenical Centre

places.name: Aso Rock
places.what: Aso Rock is a granite inselberg that dominates the skyline of Abuja. It was the reference point of the city's first concept plan and takes its name from the community that lived around it.

facts.label: Planning role
facts.value: Reference point for the first concept plan of the city by International Planning Associates

source.title: The contemporary and historical Aso Rock
source.author: Umar Shuaibu
source.quote: the Aso Rock was used as the reference point while drawing the first concept plan for the development of the city by the International Planning Associates (IPA)

facts.label: Geology
facts.value: Described as the most prominent granite inselberg and the most dramatic and easily recognised feature within the Federal Capital City

source.title: The Natural Landmarks Of Abuja And National Monuments
source.quote: The Aso Hill is the most prominent granite inselberg, the most dramatic and easily recognized feature within the FCC

facts.label: Visibility
facts.value: Dominates the view for as much as twenty miles

source.title: The Natural Landmarks Of Abuja And National Monuments
source.quote: The Aso Hill dominates view for as much as twenty miles

facts.label: Name
facts.value: Derived from the name of the original community around it, the Gwandara of Aso

source.title: The contemporary and historical Aso Rock
source.author: Umar Shuaibu
source.quote: The Aso Rock derived its name from the name of the original community inhabiting the area surrounding it

myth.claim: Abuja was an empty 'no man's land' before it was chosen as the capital.
myth.truth: The site was inhabited by several ethnic groups including the Gbagyi, Koro, Gade and Gwandara; the Gbagyi say they were the original settlers and have continued to fight for the land.

source.title: Nigeria@60: Why Nigeria's capital was moved from Lagos to Abuja
source.author: Lois Ugbede
source.quote: Abuja was a site in the center of the country inhabited by several ethnic groups like the Gbagyi, Koro, Gade, and Gwandara

notNotFound: Population is the 2006 census figure for Abuja Municipal Area Council (the council area containing the city), not a delimited 'city proper'; no later census exists.

National Mosque: sources conflict on dates (Tribune: completed 1984; Daily Trust: designed, built and commissioned in Babangida's era, which began in 1985); only the 1984 and 1981 statements are recorded, the conflict is unresolved.
National Christian Centre: dedication date, architect and capacity could not be verified in a readable non-travel source; facts rest on one Daily Trust opinion piece.
Economy and culture facts about Abuja city itself were not recorded for lack of a readable institutional source.
Osun-Osogbo is in Osogbo, Osun State, not in Abuja; UNESCO page unreadable so facts come from CNN and the grove's trust.
